strategy_title: Fix 1D Grid Bug Silently Skipping Y-Dimension Rows
strategy_description: When a Triton kernel uses tl.program_id(1) and tl.program_id(2) for Y-dimension iteration but is launched with a 1D grid, all Y-program-IDs are always 0, silently computing only the first YBLOCK rows of a much larger tensor. The fix is to extend the launch grid to 2D: (cdiv(xnumel, XBLOCK), cdiv(ynumel, YBLOCK)), ensuring all Y-rows are covered. The profiling signal for this bug is grid_size << sm_count (e.g., 16 vs 132 SMs), waves_per_sm ~0.01, and achieved occupancy far below theoretical (6.2% vs 100%), with the LaunchConfiguration NCU rule flagging the mismatch.
slow_pseudocode:
# 1D grid — Y-dimension never iterated
YBLOCK = 8
XBLOCK = 128
grid = (cdiv(xnumel, XBLOCK),)  # = (16,) — tl.program_id(1) always 0
kernel[grid](in_ptr0, in_ptr1, out_ptr0, ynumel, xnumel, YBLOCK, XBLOCK)
fast_pseudocode:
# 2D grid — covers all ynumel Y-rows
YBLOCK = 32
XBLOCK = 128
grid = (cdiv(xnumel, XBLOCK), cdiv(ynumel, YBLOCK))  # = (1, 67600)
kernel[grid](in_ptr0, in_ptr1, out_ptr0, ynumel, xnumel, YBLOCK, XBLOCK)
applicable_when: Triton kernel uses tl.program_id(1) or tl.program_id(2) for Y/Z-dimension indexing but the launch grid is 1D; LaunchConfiguration NCU rule fires with grid_size << sm_count; waves_per_sm < 0.1; achieved occupancy < 10% while theoretical is 100%.
do_not_apply_when: Kernel is intentionally 1D (no Y/Z program_id usage); grid is already multi-dimensional; the small grid is intentional due to small problem size.
framework_notes: Triton-specific: grid must be a tuple matching the number of program_id dimensions used in the kernel body. If the kernel calls tl.program_id(1), the grid tuple must have at least 2 elements. The speedup here (1.05x) is modest because the profiling was done on a very small workload (2048 threads total); the correctness fix matters more than the measured speedup — the kernel was silently computing wrong results on all but the first YBLOCK rows.
